methodology: Aggressive dedup across 14 unit deep JSONs (~470 unit-level concept entries collapsed to 56 canonical CONCEPTs + 12 POSITIONs). Tier-1 reserved for the volume's primary apparatus (5 pentad terms; 10 dyadic ratios; 4 master tropes; representative-anecdote; circumference; substance-vocabulary load-bearers; symbolic-action; transformation-of-terms; merger/division; scapegoat-dialectic; temporizing-of-essence; Socratic transcendence; action-vs-motion; consubstantial substance; god-term; philosophic-school featuring; grammar-vs-idiom; common-ground/pentad-overlaps; ratios-reversibility; ratios-as-principles; incipient act/attitude; paradox-of-substance; paradox-of-purity; actus-status; intrinsic-extrinsic; universal-monetary substance). Tier-2 reserved for chapter-central concepts deployed in ≥2 chapters (e.g. ambiguity-as-resource, two-points-of-departure, ground-double-usage, pathetic-fallacy extended, poiema-pathema-mathema, rhetorical substance). Tier-3 reserved for distinctive apparatuses developed in one chapter but elevated to book-level relevance (Edenic paradigm, demonic trinity, dissolution-of-drama).

concepts.label: Dramatism (method-name)
concepts.gloss: Burke's titular method-name: motives analyzed in a perspective developed from the analysis of drama, treating language and thought primarily as modes of action rather than modes of representation. The Grammar is the foundational volume of a projected dramatistic trilogy (Grammar / Rhetoric / Symbolic).

concepts.label: The pentad (five key terms of dramatism)
concepts.gloss: Act / Scene / Agent / Agency / Purpose — the five irreducible terms of motive-statement, offered as the generating principle of dramatistic analysis. Each term answers a single interrogative (what / where-or-when / who / how / why). The pentad is a system of placement rather than a historical survey; transcendental rather than formal (Kantian in scope).

concepts.label: Act (pentad term)
concepts.gloss: The pentad term answering 'what was done?' On the scholastic-realist construal Burke develops in GM-06, an act is an actualization (energeia) — the bringing of a potentiality into realization in accordance with a form proper to its kind. Distinguishable from mere motion (which lies in the realm of instruments); admits a spectrum (attitude, incipient act, delayed act) and is reciprocally related to potency. Featured by Realism (Aristotle/Aquinas).

concepts.label: Scene (pentad term)
concepts.gloss: The pentad term answering 'where/in what situation?' Names the background, setting, situation, or containing environment within which an act occurs and an agent moves. As containing-principle for action, scene fixes the circumference within which motive may be located. Featured by Materialism (Hobbes, Spinoza, Darwin, Lucretius, Stoicism). Spinoza's universal substance is the maximal-circumference instance.

concepts.label: Agent (pentad term)
concepts.gloss: The pentad term answering 'who did it?' Names the constituting subject — the doer of the act, from which (on idealist construal) scene, act, agency, and purpose are derived. Admits subdivision into co-agents and counter-agents and generalization into super-agents (church, race, nation, Spirit, class). Featured by Idealism (Berkeley, Hume, Leibniz, Kant, Hegel) — and by Marxism as a hybrid 'idealistic materialist' (class-as-collective-agent under materialist surface).

concepts.label: Agency (pentad term)
concepts.gloss: The pentad term answering 'how? by what means?' Names the instruments, methods, and mediating media through which an act is performed. Paradigmatic in tools, machines, and the pragmatist nesting of file/hand/brain/educational-system. Featured by Pragmatism (James, Dewey, Mead, Peirce, Bridgman) — the modern, science-driven inversion of Aristotle's subordination of agency under final cause: 'means become ancestors of ends.'

concepts.label: Purpose (pentad term)
concepts.gloss: The pentad term answering 'why?' Names the end, telos, motivating-toward-which of an act. The term most subject to violent disagreement among motive-attributors. Featured by Mysticism (Plotinus, Plato's Good=One, Bonaventura, Christian mystics) — recognizable not by mere unity but by 'unity of the individual with some cosmic or universal Purpose.' Most susceptible to dissolution: pure Purpose collapses into the paradox of substance (docta ignorantia) and survives implicitly even where formally eliminated.

concepts.label: Scene-act ratio
concepts.gloss: The dyadic ratio whereby the quality of the scene implies (contains, calls forth) a correspondingly qualified act, and convertibly the act demands or constructs a scene of corresponding quality. Reversible; usable deterministically or hortatorily. The chapter-titular ratio of GM-01 'Container and Thing Contained' and the prediction-engine of dramatistic analysis (Burke's deployment in the Keats Ode worked example, GM-10).

concepts.label: Scene-agent ratio
concepts.gloss: The dyadic ratio whereby person and place stand in synecdochic correspondence: the quality of a place implies a corresponding quality of inhabitant; the contents of a divine container share in its divinity. Positional in the strong sense (scene contains agent). Worked at length in nineteenth-century idealist 'Einklang zwischen Innen- und Aussenwelt' and in the naturalist-novelist embarrassment (brutalizing scene yields brutal characters).

concepts.label: Scene-agency ratio
concepts.gloss: The dyadic ratio between scene and the instrumental means employed in an act. The scene affords/constrains which agencies are available; conversely, new agencies (technologies, methods) accumulate to become scenic — Burke's Biddle example: railroad, telegraph, telephone, automobile, radio 'having in their accumulation become scenic' motivate political acts.

concepts.label: Scene-purpose ratio
concepts.gloss: The dyadic ratio between scene and the purpose toward which an act tends. A scene affords particular purpose-structures (quest-givers, eschatological horizons, providential cosmos); conversely a purpose may project a scene proportioned to it. Hegelian Reason-as-Grundprinzip is its paradigm idealist deployment; the Stoic cosmic-providential plan is its materialist (pronoia) deployment.

concepts.label: Act-agent ratio
concepts.gloss: The dyadic ratio between an act and the agent who performs it. NOT a strict containment relation: 'the agent does not contain the act, though its results might be said to pre-exist virtually within him.' Temporal/sequential: agents author acts; acts can in turn make or remake the agent. Burke's signature examples: 'sobering influence of the Presidency,' judicial robes, Russian wartime resistance (act-agent vs scene-act as competing readings). Scholastic-realist primary ratio: 'every thing acts according as it is in act' (Aquinas).

concepts.label: Act-agency ratio
concepts.gloss: The dyadic ratio between act and the instrumental means employed to perform it. Burke's way-words discussion (hodos / tao / yoga / dike → met-hodos as method-as-means) is the chapter's clearest formulation of the act/agency boundary instability: an act-word (way of life) becomes an agency-word (means of doing) by a subtle slide from being to doing.

concepts.label: Act-purpose ratio
concepts.gloss: The dyadic ratio between act and the purpose toward which it tends. An act is consummated only insofar as it realizes the purpose for the sake of which it is done; conversely a purpose is articulate only insofar as it admits expression in a concrete act. The Aeschylean Erinyes→Eumenides transformation is Burke's paradigm of act-purpose total transformation.

concepts.label: Agent-agency ratio
concepts.gloss: The dyadic ratio between an agent and the instrumental means available to (or characteristic of) that agent. Agent-character implies a corresponding set of fit agencies; conversely, habituated agencies constitute the agent's character. The Seurat-pointillism case (book p. 8) is a borderline instance where the medium becomes the common element relating agent to scene.

concepts.label: Agent-purpose ratio
concepts.gloss: The dyadic ratio between an agent and the purpose toward which the agent's action tends. Burke locates 'needs' as 'a property of agents,' making agent-purpose the relation between an agent's needs/wants/aspirations and the purposes they generate. Distinguishes 'primal needs' (proper to agent) from 'new needs' (which may best be treated as scenic).

concepts.label: Agency-purpose ratio
concepts.gloss: The dyadic ratio between the instrumental means and the purpose for which they are employed. Agency tends to acquire its own teleology under sustained use ('philosophy of means'); purpose conversely shapes which agencies are admissible. The chapter-titular ratio of GM-07; the dialectical hinge between Pragmatism (Agency-feature) and Mysticism (Purpose-feature). Burke's 'Mysticism of Means' critique (Huxley pacifism) is its most worked instance.

concepts.label: Reversibility of ratios (10 → 20)
concepts.gloss: Burke's principle (GM-01, GM-06) that each ratio operates in both directions: scene-act reads either as scene-implies-act or as act-demands-scene; the ten dyadic ratios expand to twenty reversible ratios. 'A ratio is a formula indicating a transition from one term to another'; the mediated necessarily differs from the immediate, as translation differs from original. The 1962 Addendum (GM-09) sharpens: order of terms matters (scene-act ≠ act-scene).

concepts.label: Ratios as principles of determination / selectivity
concepts.gloss: Burke's strong formulation: the ratios are 'principles of determination' — the analytical engine of dramatism, not merely a catalogue. Softened reading: principles of selectivity (a situation 'votes for' appropriate temperaments and acts rather than producing them ex nihilo; 'mute inglorious Miltons' as unselected seeds). The choice between competing ratios is rhetorically consequential — ratio-selection deflects attention from one motive-locus to another.

concepts.label: Metaphor / perspective (master trope)
concepts.gloss: The device for seeing something in terms of something else — bringing out the thisness of a that. Literal-realistic substitution: perspective. To consider A from the point of view of B is to use B as a perspective on A. Reality is not dissolved by multi-perspectivism; it is established by it. Degrees of being correspond to variety-of-perspectives-supportable (plants > minerals; animals > plants; men > animals).

concepts.label: Metonymy / reduction (master trope)
concepts.gloss: Conveying an incorporeal or intangible state in terms of the corporeal or tangible ('heart' for 'emotions'); the 'archaicizing' device. Reduction is the one-direction (quality-to-quantity) special case proper to scientific realism. Two senses: poet's metonymy as figure/symbolization vs. scientific behaviorist's metonymy as substantial reduction. The trope underwrites materialism's scene-featuring.

concepts.label: Synecdoche / representation (master trope)
concepts.gloss: Convertibility between two terms in an integral relationship: part for whole, whole for part, container for contained, sign for signified, cause for effect, genus for species, and all reversals. The 'noblest synecdoche' is microcosm-macrocosm identity (Leibniz). Two-way (unlike metonymy's one-way). Burke extends to before/after, implicit/explicit, name/narrative, disease/cure, hero/villain, active/passive. Underwrites every representative-anecdote choice.

concepts.label: Irony / dialectic (master trope)
concepts.gloss: Arises when one tries, by the interaction of terms upon one another, to produce a development that uses all the terms. From the standpoint of this total form ('perspective of perspectives'), no participating sub-perspective is precisely right or precisely wrong; all are voices integrally affecting one another. True/classic/humble irony is grounded in consubstantiality with the 'enemy' (Flaubert, Mann, Newton, Falstaff); romantic/Pharisaic irony is grounded in superiority. The over-all formula: A → non-A (the peripety).

concepts.label: Paradox of substance
concepts.gloss: The structural irony at the root of all substance-talk: the word designates what a thing intrinsically is, but etymologically refers to something outside the thing that stands beneath or supports it (sub-stance, hypostasis, stā- root). Every substance-claim covertly imports a contextual reference into an intrinsic claim. The master-irony of GM-02 from which the substance-vocabulary taxonomy is derived; recapitulated as a dialectical staple in GM-09.

concepts.label: Contextual / geometric substance
concepts.gloss: Definition by placement of a thing within its context, location, or surroundings. To define (de-finire) is to mark boundaries, requiring reference to what is outside the thing. Maximalist version: Spinoza's universal substance, where each object is determined by the totality (omnis determinatio est negatio). Geometric subspecies: Euclidean-Spinozistic implicit-relation calculus.

concepts.label: Familial (tribal, ancestral) substance
concepts.gloss: Defining a substance by ancestral cause — biological descent or spiritualized analogue (covenant, founder, eponym, creation). Includes Plato's archetypal Forms (each thing imitating its eponym in heaven) and Aristotle's entelechy (the individual as actualization of its class). Mediaeval universalia debate (ante rem / in re / post rem) is its scholastic refraction.

concepts.label: Directional substance
concepts.gloss: Substance characterized by motion toward, by 'the way,' by direction-from-within. Strongly futuristic and purposive ('Where are you going?' rather than 'Where are you from?'). Includes the cluster motion / movement / cause / emotion / moment as variant glosses on motivation.

concepts.label: Dialectic substance
concepts.gloss: The over-all substance category: substance arising from the systematic contemplation of antinomies — recognition that we necessarily define a thing in terms of something else, where the something else is the other (the antagonist, the agon). The dramatistic super-category that subsumes contextual / familial / directional / geometric substance-types.

concepts.label: Paradox of purity (pure substance flips to its negation)
concepts.gloss: When a substance is purified by abstraction to its absolute, it tends toward its negation: God as 'pure person' is impersonal; pure being is not-being (Hegel); pure escape is perpetual imprisonment in escape; Aristotle's God as Pure Act = eternal repose. Plotinus's negative theology arrives at abstract Oneness by negating all material attributes.

concepts.label: Actus / status (action-state dyad)
concepts.gloss: Burke's load-bearing dyadic reduction of the tragic triad (poiema/pathema/mathema): act vs. state, motion vs. rest, drama vs. lyric, faith-as-act vs. knowledge-as-state. Maps onto potentiality/actuality and tracks the philological drift by which active terms (aretē, virtus, hero) become state-terms ('L'état c'est moi'). Articulates the substance vocabulary with the Act-Agent ratio of the pentad.

concepts.label: Intrinsic / extrinsic substance
concepts.gloss: The dialectical pairing of motivations-within-the-agent against motivations-derived-from-scene. Hegel pairs Matter (extrinsic, gravity-externally-referred) with Spirit (intrinsic, Bei-sich-selbst-sein). The poles invert structurally when an intrinsic principle is operationalized through external means. The intrinsic must not be confused with the unique. GM-11 generalizes this as the scope-of-text question and resolves it via the poem-as-act framework.

concepts.label: Rhetorical substance
concepts.gloss: The ambiguity of substance as a deployable resource of persuasion. 'Substantially,' 'essentially,' 'in principle,' 'in the long run' allow a speaker to assert identity at a level of generality that cannot be falsified by particulars. Positivists who outlaw substance reimport it covertly under 'in-principle' and 'universally valid.'

concepts.label: Consubstantial substance (epithetic, identificatory)
concepts.gloss: Substance as it operates in epithets and identification-tactics: to call a man brother is to proclaim consubstantiality; to call him bastard is to attack his familial 'authorship.' An epithet assigns substance doubly — characterizes the object and implies an action toward it, thus serving as motive. Forward-anchors the consubstantiation/identification apparatus of A Rhetoric of Motives (1950).

concepts.label: Universal motive / monetary substance (money as god-term)
concepts.gloss: When a substance becomes a universal motive, it operates as a master scene supplying believers with a common motivational ground. Monotheism and the monetary motive are structurally parallel; money 'transubstantiates' from agency (medium of exchange) into ground/purpose of action — the 'capitalist psychosis.' GM-08 develops money as God-term of constitutional frames ('where one can volunteer, there one is free').

concepts.label: Representative anecdote
concepts.gloss: The compact case that condenses the analytical pattern Burke will then expand into a full terminology; the form 'in conformity with which the vocabulary is constructed.' A good representative anecdote is to a vocabulary of motives what a paradigm is to a research program — its scope-limiter and its generative seed. Drama is Burke's representative anecdote for human motives; behaviorist conditioned reflex is the negative example. GM-13 contrasts representative vs. reductive anecdote.

concepts.label: Circumference (scope of scene)
concepts.gloss: The analyst's elected scope-of-scene; the size of the contextual frame within which an act is located. Burke's most transferable methodological construct after the pentad itself. Selection of circumference 'is in itself an act, an act of faith.' Different circumferences yield different motives for the same act. The historical narrowing-of-circumference (God's law → natural law → environment → monetary scene) is Burke's structural account of secularization.

concepts.label: Action vs. motion (Dramatistic distinction)
concepts.gloss: Any verb with connotations of consciousness or purpose falls under 'act'; stumbling over an obstruction is not act but mere motion; the basic Dramatistic unit is 'the human body in conscious or purposive motion.' Behaviorism truncates drama by reducing action to motion. The watershed-moment dividing dramatist from operationalist vocabularies (GM-06): no instrument can record action ('ideas') except insofar as the subject-matter is reduced to motion.

concepts.label: Symbolic action
concepts.gloss: Language considered as a mode of action (poetic) rather than information (scientific); a poem is the symbolic act of its maker, which the reader re-enacts in reading. Symbolic action is the realm of the incipient/attitudinal par excellence — actual conflicts can be transcended there, with results sometimes fatal, sometimes felicitous. Burke's central concept for analyzing literary works and rhetorical performances as motivated acts.

concepts.label: Incipient act / attitude (proto-sixth-term)
concepts.gloss: An incipient act is a perception/attitude that contains the form of a not-yet-actualized act — Richards' 'preliminary adjustments, getting ready to act' or Mead's 'beginnings of acts.' Fundamentally ambiguous: an attitude can be SUBSTITUTE for an act OR FIRST STEP toward an act. Forward-anchors the sixth pentad term Burke adds in the 1962 Addendum (GM-09) and develops fully in A Rhetoric of Motives (1950). Keats's Urn-as-'fair Attitude' is the summational lyric instance.

concepts.label: Featuring of a term (philosophic-school diagnostic)
concepts.gloss: Burke's diagnostic move: each philosophic school selects one of the five terms as Ausgangspunkt (generating principle) and develops a vocabulary suited to give that term full expression, with the other four slighted or placed in its perspective. Materialism features Scene; Idealism features Agent; Realism features Act; Pragmatism features Agency; Mysticism features Purpose. The diagnostic is featuring, not exclusivity — every philosophy deploys all five terms.

concepts.label: Grammar vs. philosophic idiom (universal vs. open)
concepts.gloss: Burke's signature two-level claim: a statement of the grammatical principles of motivation can lay claim to universal validity (every motive-attribution must reference some background, etc.), but the choice of any particular philosophic idiom filling in those principles (God / nature / history / means of production for Scene) is open to question and varies with cultural situation. A philosophy is a casuistry of the pentadic resources.

concepts.label: Transformation of terms (master dialectical apparatus)
concepts.gloss: Master apparatus of GM-09 and pervasive throughout the Grammar: tracking the disposition and trans-position of terms across motive-statements; the way ancestral, derivative, and bridge terms migrate, merge, split, or get re-keyed under dialectical pressure. Burke's signature methodological move — pentad as a generating principle whose transformations, permutations, and combinations produce the full variety of motive-statements.

concepts.label: Merger and division
concepts.gloss: The two fundamental dialectical operations (Plato, Phaedrus): merger = comprehension of scattered particulars in one idea; division = carving an idea at the joints. Most concrete dialectical events are mergers atop division or divisions atop merger; a 'third / pontificating term' (continuity, polarity, synthesis) is usually generated to mediate. Per genus et differentiam is the classical instance: merger via genus + division via differentia.

concepts.label: Dialectic of the scapegoat
concepts.gloss: Three-step ritual by which a charismatic vicar absorbs and carries off the collective iniquities of a community: (1) original merger — iniquities shared between iniquitous and chosen vessel; (2) ritualistic division — alienation of the shared element onto the vessel; (3) new merger — purified community defined in dialectical opposition to the sacrificial offering. The scapegoat is consubstantial with persecutors. Hitlerite Anti-Semitism is the cleanest negative example; Socrates as scapegoat of transcendence is the closing application.

concepts.label: Temporizing of essence
concepts.gloss: The pun on sequence: the logically prior can be expressed as the temporally prior, and vice versa. Essence becomes narrated as a 'going back' to origins (Freud's primal horde, Plato's Meno-recollection, original sin); historicist and essentialist vocabularies are convertible. Translation rule: when an apparently empirical-historical claim is discredited as fact, ask whether it was really a statement about essence. Ibsen's Peer Gynt is GM-09's worked case.

concepts.label: Socratic transcendence (Upward Way)
concepts.gloss: The upward dialectical move: a new motive discovered en route; the position at the end is reached by transformation, and the position at the start can only retrospectively be seen in light of the new motivation. Burke's signature reading: a Platonic dialogue is an ACT of transcendence (Phaedrus' five levels), not just a plea for one. Plotinus's journey 'to the Primal-Principle' is the mystical instance; Korzybski's higher-and-higher levels of generalization is the modern semantic instance.

concepts.label: Pentad overlap / common ground / margins of transformability
concepts.gloss: The five pentad terms participate in a common ground or substance, whose role as their causal ancestor makes them transformable into one another at every point where their fields overlap. The 'great central moltenness' / alchemic alembic figure (GM-00): distinctions arise from a central moltenness where all is merged. The fingers-and-palm metaphor: terms distinct at the extremities merge in the palm of the hand. This pliancy is what licenses grand-style metaphysical reduction-to-one (being / action / motion as titular over-all terms).

concepts.label: Ambiguity as resource (not defect)
concepts.gloss: Burke's methodological signature: where logical positivism and symbolic logic seek terms free of ambiguity, the Grammar wants terms that clearly reveal the strategic spots at which ambiguities necessarily arise, because the areas of ambiguity are exactly where transformations among the terms take place. Ambiguities are alchemic opportunities, not defects.

concepts.label: Consistent / compensatory points of departure
concepts.gloss: A pentad term used as 'principle' admits two opposite developmental directions. Consistent: derive consequences from the term's nature ('reasons by a therefore'). Compensatory: depart toward the term's near-antithesis ('reasons by a however'). Lets a thinker keep a god-term while diverging from it ('naturalism' begun as man-in-nature becoming name for technology-and-money).

concepts.label: God-term
concepts.gloss: The over-all summarizing term in a vocabulary — the universal title to which all less general terms are related as parts to whole. 'Being,' 'God,' 'money,' 'freedom' are Burke's leading examples. Designates 'the ultimate motivation, or substance, of a Constitutional frame' (GM-08). Faraday's unified-energy formula as 'perfect god-term' / Title of Titles (GM-09).

concepts.label: Ground (background / reason double-usage)
concepts.gloss: The philosophical term 'ground' carries the double sense of background (scene) and reason (cause). Hegelian idealism exploits this by positing Reason as the Grundprinzip — at once mover of history and substance of which history is made. Leveraged in GM-10's reading of the theological controversy about whether God willed the good because it is good, or the good is good because God willed it.

concepts.label: Pathetic fallacy / motion-action ambiguity (extended)
concepts.gloss: Ruskin's term (attribution of human emotions to non-human objects: 'the trees were gay, the mountains mourned') interpreted by Burke as tracking the scene-agent (or LYRIC) ratio. Burke extends to cover the broader 'action-motion ambiguity' (motion-personalization-as-act): 'the wheat tossed in the wind' is motion; 'the wheat tossed its head in the wind' is action. The watershed moment dividing dramatism from operationalism.

concepts.label: Poiema / pathema / mathema (tragic-dialectic triad)
concepts.gloss: Burke's Greek-grammar triplet of action / suffering / learning. Greek proverb ta pathemata mathemata ('the suffered is the learned'). The tragic pattern: action (poiema) calls forth a counter-assertion from its context that the agent suffers (pathema); from the suffered comes knowledge (mathema) that transcends the original act. Christian martyrdom: act-of-self-sacrifice identical with sufferance; pathema (temptation) + poiema (resistance) + mathema (understanding) = martyrdom as new action-passion level.

concepts.label: Edenic paradigm (total acts producing total transformations)
concepts.gloss: If an agent acts in keeping with his nature (act-agent), changing his scene (scene-act), and likening agent to scene (scene-agent), the result is a state of mutual conformity — an Edenic paradigm applicable only to total acts producing total transformations. Theological notions of creation and re-creation approach this limit (Striegel's reading of Christ's work on the Cross; Aeschylus' Erinyes becoming Eumenides).

concepts.label: Demonic trinity (erotic + urinary + excremental cluster)
concepts.gloss: Burke's image-cluster for the cloacal-mystical: three bodily principles vicariously substitutable for one another (rain ↔ urination ↔ erotic-purpose); 'thinking of the body' as condition of poetic transcendence; ecclesia super cloacam. Mystic thoroughness requires recognition of fundamental taboos at the very moment of their transcendence.

concepts.label: Dissolution of drama (four ways)
concepts.gloss: The dramatistic perspective contains a point at which it abolishes itself in its own enunciation. Four canonical paths: (1) drama dissolves into lyric state; (2) action reduced to motion (scientism); (3) philosophies OF dramatism — Burke's own move — coordinates derived from drama yet used non-dramatically; (4) philosophies of super-drama — monotheistic god as super-person becomes impersonal.

positions.claim: Motives are grammatical-terministic, not psychological-empirical: any complete statement about motive must answer all five pentadic questions (what / where-or-when / who / how / why); what differs across cases is not the questions but the values assigned and the foregrounded term.

Grammatical principles of motivation may claim universal validity (every motive-statement must reference some background, etc.); particular philosophic idioms filling in those principles (God / nature / environment / history / means of production for Scene) are open to question and vary with cultural situation.
positions.critique_target: any one philosophic idiom claiming uniquely-correct ontology of motive; symbolic logic and logical positivism's universalist terminological ambitions

positions.claim: Where logical positivism / symbolic logic seek to abolish terminological ambiguity, the Grammar wants terms that clearly reveal where ambiguity necessarily arises, because ambiguity is the precondition of transformation among the terms; ambiguities are alchemic opportunities, not defects.
positions.critique_target: symbolic logic and logical positivism; polemical idol-smashing of one-philosophic-term-as-too-ambiguous

positions.claim: The five terms are mutually transformable because they participate in a common ground or substance; their pliancy across the margins of overlap is the analytic engine of dramatism; metaphysical systems exploit this pliancy by reducing the five to one and deducing the others from it as causal descendants.
positions.critique_target: grand-style metaphysical reduction-to-one (being / action / motion / development / experience as titular over-all terms); implicit No-Metaphysics reduction to atomic constituent ('X is nothing but Y' unmasking)

positions.claim: The ratios are 'principles of determination' (and in softened reading, principles of selectivity): they are the analytical engine of dramatism, not merely a catalogue. Every coherent motive-statement is implicitly a claim about which ratio is operative; ratio-selection is a strategic move within the Rhetoric of Motives.
positions.critique_target: term-by-term readings of dramatism that miss the ratio-structure; essentialist motive-vocabularies that ignore the implicit ratio-logic in their own usage

positions.claim: Substance is structurally paradoxical, not eliminable: the paradox of substance is inherent in the act of definition itself — any term for what a thing intrinsically is must, etymologically and grammatically, refer at least implicitly to what is outside the thing. Banishing the term merely conceals its functions; substantiation is observable structural reality, not illusion.
positions.critique_target: twentieth-century positivism and operationalism (which outlaw substance but reimport it under 'in principle' / 'universally valid')

positions.claim: Act is a non-reducible locus of motives; every act contains an irreducible 'modicum of novelty' or 'magic' that cannot be relocated under Scene, Agent, Agency, or Purpose without remainder. Creation is the paradigm act (causa sui).
positions.critique_target: behaviorist / operationalist reductions of act to motion; pantheistic collapse of agent-scene-act into a single ground

positions.claim: The selection of a circumference is itself an act, an 'act of faith,' and is the constitutive (not merely preliminary) move of any motive-analysis. Choice of where to draw the scope-of-scene boundary determines what counts as motivationally relevant.
positions.critique_target: any methodology that treats scope-selection as theoretically neutral preliminary

positions.claim: Each major philosophic school is generated by featuring one pentad term as motive-locus: Materialism features Scene (Hobbes/Spinoza/Darwin/Hellenistic materialisms); Idealism features Agent (Berkeley/Hume/Leibniz/Kant/Hegel; with Marxism as 'idealistic materialist' hybrid); Realism features Act (Aristotle/Aquinas); Pragmatism features Agency (James/Dewey/Mead/Bridgman); Mysticism features Purpose (Plotinus/Plato Good=One/Bonaventura).
positions.critique_target: essentialist readings of philosophic schools as defined by surface-vocabulary rather than featured-term diagnosis

positions.claim: Marxism is best translated as 'idealistic materialist': despite materialist surface vocabulary, its motive-locus is the class-as-collective-agent, and its futuristic stress on social unification + constant call upon human agents is intensely idealistic. Dialectical materialism requires agenthood permeating scene (Lenin's property-similar-to-sensation).
positions.critique_target: vulgar-materialist readings of Marx; Hobbesian-mechanistic readings; Hegel as antithetical-source

positions.claim: The four master tropes (metaphor / metonymy / synecdoche / irony) are operations for the discovery and description of 'the truth,' not figures of speech. Their literal-realistic substitutions are perspective / reduction / representation / dialectic. Any one trope fully developed generates the other three. The tropes operate as a parallel apparatus to the pentad.
positions.critique_target: the figurative-usage tradition (Quintilian-Cicero-Richards-Ogden) that subordinates tropes to ornamentation

positions.claim: True irony is humble and consubstantial; romantic irony is Pharisaic and superior — and only the first deserves the name. The dialectic of irony requires that the analyst be 'simultaneously both outside the criminal and within him' (Newton on the criminal; Flaubert: 'Madame Bovary, c'est moi'; Mann's 'Judas psychology').
positions.critique_target: Allen Tate's reading of Eliot's Waste Land as 'humility' (Burke calls it Pharisaic); romantic irony as artist-superior-to-rejected-role

deduplication_flags_worth_noting: C-RATIOS-REVERSIBLE consolidates GM-01's reversibility principle, GM-06's potential-to-actual ratio formula (10→20), and GM-09's 1962-Addendum ratio-order-matters clarification — three distinct but converging formulations of the same insight.

C-SUBSTANCE-ACTUS-STATUS is canonical because it spans GM-02 (substance-vocabulary origin), GM-06 (Act-Agent ratio anchor via passive forms in Indo-European grammar), and GM-09 (action-passion pair derivation + constitutions-survive-enactments cross-link).

C-INCIPIENT-ACT-ATTITUDE is the proto-sixth-term: present as forward-flag in GM-01 (Attitude as incipient/symbolic act), developed phenomenologically in GM-06 (Richards/Mead/Korzybski cluster), embodied in GM-07 (the 'attitude, the incipient act' of the coin-tossed-to-leper), modeled lyrically in GM-10 (Keats's 'fair Attitude'), generalized methodologically in GM-11 (lyric-as-arrested-act), and explicitly proposed as 6th pentad term in the GM-09 1962 Addendum.

C-SUBSTANCE-UNIVERSAL-MONETARY consolidates the money-as-god-term thread across GM-02 (universal-motive-substance origin), GM-03 (monetary-reduction long case study + money-as-substitute-for-God), GM-07 ('Catholic act, Protestant agent, Scientist scene' with money across), and GM-08 (money as God-term of constitutional frames).

C-PHILOSOPHIC-SCHOOL-FEATURING is the master diagnostic spanning GM-04 (Materialism→Scene), GM-05 (Idealism→Agent), GM-06 (Realism→Act), and GM-07 (Pragmatism→Agency + Mysticism→Purpose) — one apparatus distributed across four chapters; each chapter develops its own internal philosopher-table.

C-CONSUBSTANTIAL was kept as a single canonical concept rather than split: GM-00 introduces the proto-form via 'A may become non-A . . . consubstantial with non-A'; GM-02 names it as the consubstantial-substance type; GM-09 deploys it as the scapegoat-is-consubstantial-with-persecutors thesis; GM-13 deploys it as the foundation of classic-vs-romantic irony. All four are forward-anchors to the consubstantiation/identification apparatus of A Rhetoric of Motives (1950).

C-RATIO-AGENCY-PURPOSE consolidates the GM-01 enumeration (deferred to 'elsewhere'), the GM-07 chapter-titular dyad treatment, and the GM-04 Stoic 'bridge from Providence to pragmatism' anticipation — three loci where the same ratio is named with progressively richer development.

Attitude is NOT canonicalized as a sixth pentad term in this ontology because Burke's 1945 Grammar treats it only as proto-form (incipient-act); the explicit 6th-term proposal appears in the 1962 Addendum (GM-09) and is fully formalized only in A Rhetoric of Motives (1950). C-INCIPIENT-ACT-ATTITUDE captures the volume-internal state; the Rhetoric pipeline (future) will canonicalize Attitude proper.
